description: The property lead/deal record synced from MasterSuite PropertySummaries: one row per property lead, from raw marketing lead through purchase. Stage1/Stage2/Stage3 fields are successive underwriting evaluations of the same property — a higher stage supersedes a lower one — so 'the' ARV/budget/offer answers live in ms_property_calculations (Calculated_Arv, Calculated_ConstructionBudget, Calculated_MaxOffer, Calculated_StageMaturity).

PropertyId.meaning: Unique MasterSuite identifier for the property lead; primary key and the join key to every other ms_property_* table.
PropertyId.use_when: Joining to ms_property_calculations, status history, stage tables, or linking back to MasterSuite.

Archived.meaning: True when the property record has been archived (soft-deleted) in MasterSuite; archived rows are excluded from the sync, so this should always be false here.
Archived.do_not_use_for: Filtering dead deals — dead deals are '0 *' Status values, not Archived.

ArchivedDate.meaning: When the record was archived, if it ever was.

TerritorySlug.meaning: The franchise territory this property is assigned to (foreign key to territories); the manually-confirmed assignment.
TerritorySlug.use_when: Any per-territory rollup, filter, or franchisee-facing view.

PropertyType.meaning: Kind of property: SFR, Duplex, TownhouseCondo, Apartment, MultiFamily, Commercial, Land, Manufactured, Modular, Mobile, Lot, or Other.
PropertyType.use_when: Filtering or segmenting by property kind.

BatchId.meaning: Identifier (GUID) grouping properties that were created together in the same bulk list import.
BatchId.use_when: Tracing which import/list a lead came from.

Inserted.meaning: When the property record was first created in MasterSuite.
Inserted.use_when: Lead-age and cohort analysis (funnel velocity uses ms_property_status_history for stage timing).

InsertedBy.meaning: Username of the person (or import process) that created the record.

LastModified.meaning: When the record was last changed in MasterSuite; also drives the incremental sync.
LastModified.use_when: Checking data freshness or recent activity on a deal.

LastModifiedBy.meaning: Username of the last person who changed the record.

PropertyReviewedDate.meaning: Date the Stage 4 property review happened — the end of the analysis process, when the New Again team reviews the completed valuation, construction budget, and max offer with the franchise owner. The outcome is either a max offer to take to the seller or a decision not to make an offer.
PropertyReviewedDate.use_when: Measuring review throughput / whether a lead has been looked at.

PropertyReviewedBy.meaning: Username of the person who reviewed the lead.

PropertyReviewedByFriendlyName.meaning: Display name of the person who reviewed the lead.
PropertyReviewedByFriendlyName.use_when: Showing the reviewer's name to users.

PropertyUrl.meaning: Link to an external page for the property (e.g. a listing or auction page).
PropertyUrl.use_when: Giving users a click-through to the source listing.

AddressSlugVerbose.meaning: Normalized full-address slug (street + city + state + zip) used for de-duplication and matching.

AddressSlugShort.meaning: Shorter normalized address slug (typically street + zip) used for looser de-duplication and matching.
AddressSlugShort.use_when: Fuzzy matching when the verbose slug doesn't hit.

Streetname.meaning: Street name portion of the address (without the house number).

Zip.meaning: ZIP code of the property; also the key into zip-level market data (average price per sq ft) that drives the automatic Stage 1 ARV.
Zip.use_when: Geographic filters and zip-level market joins.

City.meaning: City of the property as entered/imported.

State.meaning: State of the property as entered/imported.

County.meaning: County of the property as entered/imported.

GoogleCity.meaning: City as returned by Google geocoding — the cleaned/canonical version of City.
GoogleCity.use_when: When you need a standardized city name for grouping.

GoogleState.meaning: State as returned by Google geocoding.

GoogleCounty.meaning: County as returned by Google geocoding.

AutoTerritorySlug.meaning: The system's automatic best-guess of the nearest territory for a property that falls outside any established territory boundary. Not authoritative for identifying a property's territory.
AutoTerritorySlug.do_not_use_for: Identifying which territory a property belongs to — always use TerritorySlug.
AutoTerritorySlug.prefer_instead: TerritorySlug (the single source of truth for a property's territory)

ZillowPropertyId.meaning: Zillow's identifier (ZPID) for the property, for linking to Zillow data.
ZillowPropertyId.use_when: Building Zillow links or joining external Zillow data.

OwnerOfferStatus.meaning: Free-text 'Owner Offer Status and History' notes — a running narrative of offers made to this owner and where negotiations stand.
OwnerOfferStatus.use_when: Summarizing negotiation history on a deal.
OwnerOfferStatus.do_not_use_for: Structured offer amounts — it is prose, not a number.

DirectSellerNotes.meaning: Free-text notes captured from conversations with a direct seller (owner who contacted NAH directly).
DirectSellerNotes.use_when: Reviewing seller conversation context on direct-seller leads.

OwnerLeadSource.meaning: How the owner/seller found or reached NAH (the marketing source of a direct-seller lead).
OwnerLeadSource.use_when: Attributing direct-seller leads to a marketing channel.

Vacant.meaning: Occupancy check from the risks review: Unchecked, Occupied, Vacant, or Unsure.
Vacant.use_when: Flagging vacant-property risk or targeting vacant properties.

Septic.meaning: Waste system check from the risks review: Sewer, Septic, or Unknown.

RoadType.meaning: Road quality in front of the property from the risks review: Yellow Line (main road), White Line, or No Line (small/unpaved road).
RoadType.use_when: Due-diligence risk review and location quality context.

LeadCategory.meaning: Top-level lead source family: Auctions, Direct Seller, Listed, Lists, Lead Mining, Referral Partners, or Other.
LeadCategory.use_when: High-level lead source segmentation and funnel reporting.

LeadType.meaning: Specific lead source within the category, e.g. Foreclosure, Tax Sale, Direct Seller, Agent Listed, REO, FSBO, PropStream, Probate, Wholesaler; the database vocabulary is broader than the constants list.
LeadType.use_when: Detailed lead-source segmentation; also drives some default rehab-grade assumptions (Tax Sale and Foreclosure have their own defaults).

LeadClassification.meaning: Legacy field originally created to distinguish tax-sale leads. Not used in several years; only relevant if NAH resumes tax sales.

LeadSubType2.meaning: Secondary lead sub-type refinement below LeadType (exact vocabulary lives in the data, not code).

ComparableSubjectCondition.meaning: The target after-repair condition of the subject property, used to select comparables that are in that same (post-renovation) condition.
ComparableSubjectCondition.use_when: Explaining how comps were filtered/adjusted for condition.

AuctionAdPrice.meaning: Price advertised in the auction listing/ad for auction leads.
AuctionAdPrice.do_not_use_for: Value estimates — it is an advertised number, not ARV.

AuctionDate.meaning: Date of the auction, stored as free text.
AuctionDate.do_not_use_for: Date math without parsing — it is text, not a date column.

AuctionTime.meaning: Time of day of the auction, stored as free text.

AuctionReserveBid.meaning: Reserve (minimum acceptable) bid published or learned for the auction.

AuctionTrustee.meaning: Name of the trustee handling the foreclosure/auction.

AuctionCountyLocation.meaning: County/location where the auction takes place (e.g. the courthouse).

AuctionDriveBy.meaning: Status indicating someone physically drove by an auction property beforehand to confirm it exists and check its condition — due diligence for tax/foreclosure auctions, where a listed house could have been demolished or missing.
AuctionDriveBy.use_when: Pulling up drive-by evidence for an auction lead.

AuctionTitle.meaning: Title-search status/notes for the auction property.

AuctionStatus.meaning: Current status of the auction itself (e.g. scheduled, postponed, cancelled, sold).
AuctionStatus.use_when: Tracking whether an auction is still happening.

Auctioneer.meaning: Name of the auction company or auctioneer running the sale.

TaxOverallGrade.meaning: Overall grade for a tax-auction property, believed to be on a 1–5 scale. Not used recently since NAH no longer runs tax auctions at scale.
TaxOverallGrade.do_not_use_for: Current analysis — dormant since tax auctions wound down.

FloodRisk.meaning: Flood-zone check from the risks review: Minimum, High, or Questionable (checked against the FEMA/flood website linked in the UI).

MethCheck.meaning: Result of checking the property against the meth-contamination registry: Passed or Failed (Failed is flagged in red in the legacy UI).

UsdaQualified.meaning: Whether the property's location qualifies for USDA rural-development financing: Qualified or Not Qualified (matters for the resale buyer pool).
UsdaQualified.use_when: Assessing resale financing options in rural markets.

GoogleSearch.meaning: Passed/Failed result of a manual Google search due-diligence check on the property, recorded in the risks review.

AedQualified.meaning: Flag for an AED program that was popular during the tax-sale era.
AedQualified.do_not_use_for: Current analysis — tied to the dormant tax-sale program.

Stage1Arv.meaning: Stage 1 (first-pass, automated) after-repair value in dollars; the engine computes it as adjusted square footage times a zip-code-based price per sq ft (or the Stage1ManualArv per-sq-ft override) and writes it back here.
Stage1Arv.use_when: Explaining the first-pass estimate or comparing stage evaluations.
Stage1Arv.do_not_use_for: Presenting as 'the ARV' — it is superseded by Stage 2/3 evaluations.
Stage1Arv.prefer_instead: ms_property_calculations.Calculated_Arv (with Calculated_StageMaturity for which stage it came from)

Stage1ManualArv.meaning: Manual override of the Stage 1 ARV price per square foot (dollars per sq ft, not a total); when set, it replaces the zip-code-derived price per sq ft in the Stage 1 ARV formula.
Stage1ManualArv.use_when: Explaining why a Stage 1 ARV differs from the zip-code default.
Stage1ManualArv.do_not_use_for: Reading as a total dollar ARV — it is per square foot.

Stage1Price.meaning: The asking price for the property (labeled 'Asking Price' in the analysis UI).
Stage1Price.use_when: Comparing our max offer to what the seller is asking.
Stage1Price.do_not_use_for: The engine's price roll-up — that is ms_property_calculations.Calculated_Price.

Stage1LocationGrade.meaning: Stage 1 location quality grade (1-5 scale) for the property's neighborhood; adjusts the zip-average price per sq ft in the Stage 1 ARV.
Stage1LocationGrade.do_not_use_for: The current location grade — Stage 2/3 grades supersede it.

Stage1RehabLevel.meaning: Stage 1 rehab severity grade on a 1-5 scale; construction budget = grade x adjusted sq ft x per-grade $/sq ft rate (ConstructionBudgetS1).
Stage1RehabLevel.do_not_use_for: Presenting as 'the construction budget' — Stage 2 grade or the Stage 3 dollar budget supersedes it.

Stage1Notes.meaning: Free-text notes from the Stage 1 evaluation.

Stage1CostOfMoneyPercent.meaning: Legacy per-property cost-of-money (financing cost) percentage captured at Stage 1; not referenced by the current calculation engine.
Stage1CostOfMoneyPercent.do_not_use_for: Dead/legacy field — not actively used; do not use it in answers.

Stage1MaxRiskFactorPercent.meaning: Legacy per-property cap on the risk factor captured at Stage 1; not referenced by the current calculation engine.
Stage1MaxRiskFactorPercent.do_not_use_for: Dead/legacy field — not actively used; do not use it in answers.

Stage1MlsSellPercent.meaning: Believed to be the commission percentage paid on the disposition (sale) side. Rarely populated/used and not relevant to answers.

LowEndPriceSquareFoot.meaning: Stage 2 comp-based low end of the market in dollars per square foot; the engine multiplies it by adjusted sq ft to show the low-end total price.
LowEndPriceSquareFoot.use_when: Showing the underwriter's low-end market bracket for the property.
LowEndPriceSquareFoot.do_not_use_for: Reading as a total price — it is per square foot.

HighEndPriceSquareFoot.meaning: Stage 2 comp-based high end of the market in dollars per square foot; multiplied by adjusted sq ft for the high-end total price.
HighEndPriceSquareFoot.use_when: Showing the underwriter's high-end market bracket for the property.
HighEndPriceSquareFoot.do_not_use_for: Reading as a total price — it is per square foot.

ArvCeiling.meaning: The upper limit on a property's ARV, set by its most limiting constraint — most often the top of the neighborhood, but it can be any constraint (e.g. only 2 bedrooms, or fronting a busy street). The ceiling is whatever the lowest such constraint dictates.
ArvCeiling.use_when: Explaining the top of the realistic resale range the underwriter set.
ArvCeiling.do_not_use_for: Presenting as the expected ARV — it is a cap, not the estimate.

OfferRange.meaning: Free-text offer range recorded on the price panel of the analysis screen (added 2020); e.g. the bracket quoted or planned for the seller.
OfferRange.use_when: Showing what offer bracket was noted for the deal.
OfferRange.do_not_use_for: Numeric offer math — it is free text; use ms_property_calculations.Calculated_MaxOffer for the engine's number.

Stage2Arv.meaning: Stage 2 (comp-based, human) ARV entered in dollars per square foot — not a total; the engine multiplies it by adjusted sq ft to get the Stage 2 ARV total, which supersedes Stage 1.
Stage2Arv.do_not_use_for: Reading as a total dollar ARV (it is per sq ft), or presenting as 'the ARV' (Stage 3 supersedes it).

Stage2Price.meaning: The seller's 'Need Price' captured at Stage 2 — what the seller says they need to get.
Stage2Price.use_when: Negotiation context: gap between seller's need and our max offer.
Stage2Price.prefer_instead: ms_property_calculations.Calculated_Price for the engine's price roll-up

Stage2LocationGrade.meaning: Stage 2 location quality grade (1-5); supersedes the Stage 1 grade in the location-grade roll-up.
Stage2LocationGrade.do_not_use_for: The current grade if a Stage 3 grade exists.

Stage2RehabLevel.meaning: Stage 2 rehab severity grade (1-5 scale); takes priority over Stage 1 and the exterior-grade total in the construction-budget formula (grade x sq ft x per-grade rate).
Stage2RehabLevel.do_not_use_for: Presenting as the construction budget — a Stage 3 dollar budget overrides everything.

Stage2Notes.meaning: Free-text notes from the Stage 2 evaluation.

Stage3ConstructionProfitRatio.meaning: Construction Profit Ratio (CPR) — a calculation, not a manual entry: for every dollar of construction spend, how much profit the deal produces. Lower is better; NAH targets a CPR of 2 or below (higher-CPR deals happen but mean working harder for the profit). A key measure in both deal analysis and territory health.

Stage3MaxOffer.meaning: Stage 3 manual override of the maximum offer in dollars; when set it replaces the engine's (ARV x risk factor) - construction budget formula, and the engine back-solves the implied risk factor from it.
Stage3MaxOffer.use_when: Explaining that leadership hand-set the max offer on this deal.
Stage3MaxOffer.do_not_use_for: Presenting as the engine's suggested offer — the system-suggested number is Calculated_MaxOffer_Original.

Stage3Arv.meaning: Stage 3 (final, human-confirmed) ARV as a total dollar amount; when set it supersedes Stage 1 and Stage 2 in the ARV roll-up.
Stage3Arv.use_when: Explaining the final ARV input on mature deals.
Stage3Arv.do_not_use_for: Answering 'what is the ARV' directly — read the roll-up instead so stage precedence is honored.

Stage3Price.meaning: Stage 3 price for the property — the negotiated/expected purchase price at the final evaluation stage.

Stage3LocationGrade.meaning: Stage 3 location quality grade (1-5); the highest-priority input to the location-grade roll-up.

Stage3RiskFactor.meaning: Stage 3 manual override of the risk factor — the fraction of ARV the deal must fit within (max offer = ARV x risk factor - construction budget); when set it replaces the engine-computed stage 1/2/3 risk factors.
Stage3RiskFactor.use_when: Explaining a hand-set risk assumption on a mature deal.
Stage3RiskFactor.do_not_use_for: Presenting as the engine's computed risk — that is Calculated_RiskFactor_Original.

Stage3ConstructionBudget.meaning: Stage 3 construction budget as an absolute dollar amount (unlike Stage 1/2 which use 1-5 rehab grades); when set it overrides the grade-based construction budget entirely.
Stage3ConstructionBudget.use_when: Explaining the final scoped rehab budget on mature deals.
Stage3ConstructionBudget.do_not_use_for: Comparing directly against Stage1/2 RehabLevel values — those are grades, not dollars.

Stage3CostOfMoneyPercent.meaning: Stage 3 per-deal cost-of-money (financing cost) percentage; today the engine only uses its presence as a signal that the deal reached Stage 3 maturity.
Stage3CostOfMoneyPercent.do_not_use_for: Financing-cost math — the engine takes financing assumptions from territory/report variables.

Stage3MaxRiskFactorPercent.meaning: Legacy Stage 3 cap on the risk factor; present in the database but not in the current entity or calculation engine.
Stage3MaxRiskFactorPercent.do_not_use_for: Dead/legacy field — not actively used; do not use it in answers.

Stage3Notes.meaning: Free-text notes from the Stage 3 evaluation; entering any counts the deal as Stage 3 mature.

Stage3MortgageStartDate.meaning: Origination date of the seller's known first mortgage, used to estimate their remaining payoff.
Stage3MortgageStartDate.use_when: Estimating seller equity / minimum viable price.
Stage3MortgageStartDate.do_not_use_for: NAH's own financing — this is the seller's loan.

Stage3MortgageAmount.meaning: Original loan amount of the seller's known first mortgage.
Stage3MortgageAmount.do_not_use_for: Current balance — the estimated remaining balance is the Calculated_Payoff field.

Stage3MortgageTerm.meaning: Term of the seller's first mortgage in number of monthly payments (360 = 30-year, 180 = 15-year).

Stage3MortgageKnownInterestRate.meaning: Known annual interest rate on the seller's first mortgage; when present it replaces the year-average rate in the payoff estimate.

Stage3Mortgage_Calculated_Payoff.meaning: Engine-estimated remaining payoff balance on the seller's first mortgage (amortized from amount, rate, term, and start date).
Stage3Mortgage_Calculated_Payoff.use_when: Estimating seller equity and the minimum price a seller could accept.
Stage3Mortgage_Calculated_Payoff.do_not_use_for: An exact payoff quote — it is an estimate.

Stage3Mortgage2StartDate.meaning: Origination date of the seller's known second mortgage, if any.
Stage3Mortgage2StartDate.use_when: Estimating seller equity when there are two liens.

Stage3Mortgage2Amount.meaning: Original loan amount of the seller's known second mortgage.
Stage3Mortgage2Amount.use_when: Estimating seller equity when there are two liens.

Stage3Mortgage2Term.meaning: Term of the seller's second mortgage in number of monthly payments.

Stage3Mortgage2KnownInterestRate.meaning: Known annual interest rate on the seller's second mortgage.

Stage3Mortgage2_Calculated_Payoff.meaning: Engine-estimated remaining payoff balance on the seller's second mortgage.
Stage3Mortgage2_Calculated_Payoff.use_when: Estimating total seller debt across both liens.
Stage3Mortgage2_Calculated_Payoff.do_not_use_for: An exact payoff quote — it is an estimate.

BuyingCost.meaning: Per-deal manual override of estimated purchase transaction costs in dollars; when empty the engine derives buying cost from territory 'quiet cost' variables.
BuyingCost.do_not_use_for: The effective buying cost — that is ms_property_calculations.Calculated_BuyingCost.

HoldingCost.meaning: Per-deal manual override of estimated holding costs (taxes, utilities, insurance while we own it) in dollars; when empty the engine derives it from territory variables.
HoldingCost.do_not_use_for: The effective holding cost — use the calculated field.

ClosingCost.meaning: Per-deal manual override of estimated resale closing costs/concessions in dollars; when empty the engine computes ARV x closing-cost percentage (capped).
ClosingCost.do_not_use_for: The effective closing cost — use the calculated field.

MlsListCost.meaning: Per-deal manual override of estimated MLS listing/selling costs (agent commissions etc.) in dollars; when empty the engine derives it from territory variables.
MlsListCost.do_not_use_for: The effective selling cost — use the calculated field.

SellDate.meaning: Purpose unclear and not actively used; appears in several tables but can be ignored.

DirectMailInitiatedDate.meaning: Date direct-mail marketing was first initiated to this property/owner.

Status.meaning: Where the lead sits in the acquisition funnel: '0 Lead List' (raw, not synced here), dead ends '0 No Offer'/'0 No Deal'/'0 Trash'/'0 Sell Later'/'0 Unresponsive', active underwriting '1' (new lead) through '2' (qualified), '3' (appointment set), '4' (made offer), then '5 Contract' and '6 Purchase' (acquired). Stages 1-4 advance automatically as evaluation fields get filled in.
Status.use_when: Any funnel, pipeline, or deal-state question; the primary deal-state field.
Status.do_not_use_for: Post-purchase project state — that is inventory status (Phase 1-5, Listed, Sold etc.) in the inventory table.

EvaluationStatus.meaning: A separate evaluation-state text field; declared on the entity but not referenced anywhere in the current application code.

BaseGrade.meaning: Base component (default 2.5) of the exterior construction-budget grade; Base + Premium + Siding + Windows + Roof + Exterior sum to the total CB grade, which acts as the rehab level when no Stage 2 rehab grade exists.
BaseGrade.use_when: Explaining how the exterior-derived rehab grade was built.
BaseGrade.do_not_use_for: Presenting as the rehab level by itself — only the summed total is used.

Premium.meaning: A construction-budget flag for properties whose characteristics push the budget significantly higher — typically foreclosures, tax sales, or long-vacant properties that carry unforeseen costs (projected because they've sat vacant). Not a marker of an upscale/high-end property.
Premium.do_not_use_for: Anything about pricing premium — it is a rehab-grade component.

Siding.meaning: Siding-condition component of the exterior construction-budget grade (points added for siding work needed).

Windows.meaning: Window-condition component of the exterior construction-budget grade (points added for window work needed).

Roof.meaning: Roof-condition component of the exterior construction-budget grade (points added for roof work needed).

ExteriorIndicators.meaning: General exterior-condition component of the construction-budget grade (points for other visible exterior issues).

SellerGender.meaning: Seller's gender, captured for negotiation/marketing context.

SellerApproxAge.meaning: Seller's approximate age bracket, captured for negotiation/marketing context.

SellerType.meaning: What kind of party the seller is: Individual/Couple, Group, Entity, or Other.

SellerRole.meaning: The seller's relationship to the property: Heir, Landlord, Owner, Investor, Lender, or Other.
SellerRole.use_when: Seller-profile segmentation (e.g. heir vs. landlord situations).

SellerMotivation.meaning: Why the seller is selling: Inheritance, Tired (landlord), Relocation, Need Cash Fast, Avoid Foreclosure, Deferred Maintenance, or Property Tax.

SellerBlackSwans.meaning: The seller's decisive hot-button (negotiation 'black swan'): Speed, Highest Cash, Flexibility, Avoid Agents, Being Taken Advantage Of, Concern for House, Probate Drama, Spouse Drama, Tenant Drama, or Tax Drama.
SellerBlackSwans.use_when: Coaching reps on what will actually close this seller.

PropertyAddressDoNotSend.meaning: Suppression flag: exclude this property address from direct-mail marketing lists (the deployment-center list generator filters on all three DoNotSend flags).
PropertyAddressDoNotSend.use_when: Any marketing-outreach decision — always honor it.

OwnerDoNotSend.meaning: Suppression flag: exclude this owner from direct-mail marketing lists.
OwnerDoNotSend.use_when: Any marketing-outreach decision — always honor it.
OwnerDoNotSend.do_not_use_for: Do not treat as clearable — these suppression flags are permanent; there is no policy to clear them.

TrusteeDoNotSend.meaning: Suppression flag: exclude the trustee contact from direct-mail marketing lists.
TrusteeDoNotSend.use_when: Any marketing-outreach decision — always honor it.

ReferralPartnerName.meaning: Name of the referral partner (e.g. Opendoor, Homelight, a wholesaler) who sent this lead.

HouseCanaryValue.meaning: The ARV that HouseCanary software projects for the property — one of NAH's more accurate ARV signals. Produced via a HouseCanary process run outside MasterSuite, based on the subject's target (post-renovation) condition, so it pulls remodeled comps and reads as a strong ARV signal.
HouseCanaryValue.use_when: Cross-checking our ARV against a third-party automated valuation.
HouseCanaryValue.do_not_use_for: Presenting as ARV — AVMs estimate current as-is value, not after-repair value.

utmMedium.meaning: Marketing attribution: the UTM medium (channel type, e.g. cpc, email) from the web form/campaign that generated the lead.
utmMedium.use_when: Marketing channel attribution for inbound leads.

utmContent.meaning: Marketing attribution: the UTM content tag (which ad/creative) from the source campaign.

utmSource.meaning: Marketing attribution: the UTM source (e.g. google, facebook) from the source campaign.

utmCampaign.meaning: Marketing attribution: the UTM campaign name from the source campaign.

MarketRiskFactor.meaning: Expected annual market-decline percentage for this deal (e.g. 10 = 10%/year), joined in from PropertyDataEntry; the engine converts it to a monthly rate and discounts the ARV over the expected buy-rehab-sell cycle time to produce the market-risk-adjusted ARV.
MarketRiskFactor.use_when: Explaining the gap between Calculated_Arv and Calculated_Arv_MarketRiskAdjusted.
MarketRiskFactor.do_not_use_for: The deal risk factor (ratio) used in max-offer math — that is a different concept (Stage3RiskFactor / Calculated_RiskFactor).

DispositionNotes.meaning: Free-text notes about the planned or actual exit strategy (disposition) for the property, joined in from PropertyDataEntry.
DispositionNotes.use_when: Reviewing exit-strategy thinking on a deal.
